name: Kaqchikel, Santa María de Jesús
world_status: statement found in a copy we already had

earlier_scan.verdict: a reachable source states the stress pattern

new_statements.quote: (p.55) El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). (p.56) El patrón de acentuación “acento en sílaba pesada” ocurren en muy pocas palabras en las variantes de Santa María de Jesús, Antigua Guatemala, Parramos, San Bartolomé Milpas Altas y Magdalena Milpas Altas. La sílaba más pesada ocurre en estructuras verbales transitivas, es la primera vocal seguida de cierre glotal (p.57) En Santa María de Jesús además de registrar la sílaba pesada: primera vocal seguida de cierre glotal, también es sílaba pesada la que tiene o se pronuncia con diptongo ie en medio de palabras
new_statements.translation: (p.55) The stress pattern in all varieties of the Kaqchikel language is fixed, its function is demarcative and its position is on the final syllable (acute or last-syllable stress). (p.56) The stress pattern 'stress on a heavy syllable' occurs in very few words in the varieties of Santa María de Jesús, Antigua Guatemala, Parramos, San Bartolomé Milpas Altas and Magdalena Milpas Altas. The heaviest syllable occurs in transitive verb structures; it is the first vowel followed by glottal closure (p.57) In Santa María de Jesús, besides registering the heavy syllable 'first vowel followed by glottal closure', a syllable that has or is pronounced with the diphthong ie in the middle of words is also heavy [and stressed]; the same results in Spanish loans that use a diphthong.
new_statements.citation: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel (ALMG); investigadores J. E. Ajsivinac Sian, Lolmay P. O. García Matzar, M. Chacach Cutzal, I. E. Alonzo Guajan. 2004. Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel: Rutzijoxik rucholik ri Kaqchikel ch'ab'al. Chimaltenango: Comunidad Lingüística Kaqchikel, Academia de Lenguas Mayas de Guatemala.
new_statements.locator: Fonología, sección 'Acento', printed pp. 55-57 (pp. 59-61); fn. 48 gives the data source as the CLK 'Variación Dialectal del Idioma Kaqchikel'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened, -, -printed pp.55-57 of ALMG/CLK 2004 Gramática descriptiva del idioma maya Kaqchikel; credits page confirms CLK-ALMG, octubre de 2004, investigadores Ajsivinac Sián, García Mátzar, Chacach Cutzal, Alonzo Guaján). All three quoted passages are on the page verbatim: p.55 'El patrón de acentuación en todas las variantes del idioma kaqchikel es fijo, su función es demarcativa y su posición es en sílaba final (acento agudo o último). Es invariable en el proceso de derivación. Por eso, no es necesaria su escritura, porque es predecible y no ejerce función distintiva.'; p.56 (b) 'El patrón de acentuación "acento en sílaba pesada" ocurren en muy pocas palabras en las variantes de Santa Mar…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the last syllable of the word in every Kaqchikel variety including Santa María de Jesús; stress is demarcative, unchanged by derivation and non-contrastive. Santa María de Jesús (with four neighbouring Sacatepéquez towns) adds a marginal weight-driven exception 'in very few words': in transitive verb forms whose first vowel is followed by a glottal stop (typically before the 3pl absolutive a'/e') that heavy syllable takes the stress (xka'rutz'ot [šká?ruc'ot] 'he will look at them', xra'xaj [šrá?šax] 'he heard it'), and in SMJ a medial syllable with the diphthong ie (from tense e, also in Spanish loans) is heavy and stressed (ato'akera [?ato?akiéro] 'handkerchief', cheja [čiéxa] 'woodpecker', axkalera [?aškaliéra] 'ladder'). Language-wide, penultimate stress also survives in a handful of native words (vakix, tukur, tata, nana, b'alam, anxa, janila) and Spanish loans (anma, paxa, alb'ertix, xalma).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned by ALMG 2004. Bennett 2018 (Glossa 3(1):67, fn.7, language-level): 'Secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel' and there is no phonotactic evidence for it.
new_statements.exceptions: p.56 (a) penultimate stress in a few native words (vakix 'cow', tukur 'owl', tata, nana, b'alam, anxa, janila 'much') and Spanish 'graves' loans (anma, paxa, alb'ertix, xalma); most varieties syncopate the second vowel of vakix/tukur/nana/tata (wakx, tukr, nan, tat), restoring final stress. p.56 (b)-p.57: SMJ/Antigua/Parramos/Milpas Altas 'acento en sílaba pesada' in very few transitive verb forms with V' before 3pl absolutive; SMJ diphthong-ie syllables and Alotenango diphthong-uo loans (maripuósa, puóbra). Loans generally keep their Spanish stress (OKMA 1997:21; CLK 2006:298).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; the ALMG rule is stated for 'la palabra' with underlined stressed syllables in citation forms, including derived and inflected verb forms. OKMA 1997:20 adds that verb/stative enclitics attract stress; Brown, Maxwell & Little 2006:138 (via Nelson 2020) add phrasal prominence on the last word of a phrase. The dialect-specific SMJ statement is based on the CLK dialect survey data (fn.48), not on instrumental measurement.
new_statements.identity_note: kaqc1276 is a Glottolog bookkeeping code for the retired ISO code cki 'Santa María de Jesús Cakchiquel', merged into Kaqchikel [cak] = kaqc1270 by ISO CR 2008-053 (2009-01-16); it is a single-municipality dialect (Santa María de Jesús, Sacatepéquez, local name Jun'ajpu'), not a separate language, so by our rule that each source is filed under the language's current Glottolog code (a retired code does not make a separate language) a catalog entry belongs under kaqc1270 (dialect note), not as a new language. The quoted ALMG 2004 statement is the language-level rule ('en todas las variantes') plus the explicit dialect-specific paragraph naming Santa María de Jesús (pp.56-57); no stress description exists that is solely about this variety. The existing kaqc1270 catalog entry rests on Berinstein 1979 (Patzicía speakers); ALMG 2004 is the more authoritative modern primary description and could supersede it.

sources.note: p.55: stress in all Kaqchikel varieties is fixed, demarcative, final ('acento agudo o último'), invariant under derivation, not written because predictable and non-distinctive. p.56 (a): penultimate stress in a few native words (vakix, tukur, tata, nana, b'alam, anxa, janila) and Spanish loans (anma, paxa, alb'ertix, xalma). p.56 (b): 'acento en sílaba pesada' in very few words only in Santa María de Jesús, Antigua Guatemala, Parramos, San Bartolomé and Magdalena Milpas Altas: in transitive verb forms the first vowel followed by glottal stop (usually before 3pl absolutive a'/e') takes stress,…

sources.citation: Nelson, Max. 2020. Right-edge prosody in Kaqchikel. Calgary Working Papers in Linguistics 31.
sources.note: Quotes Brown, Maxwell & Little 2006:138 'word stress in Kaqchikel is generally on the final syllable of a word' and 'in phrases, the primary stress falls on the last word'; acoustic examples confirm final stress, loans variable. Language-level.

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2018. Recursive prosodic words in Kaqchikel (Mayan). Glossa 3(1): 67. doi:10.5334/gjgl.550, pp.11-12 fn.7.
sources.note: Stress basically restricted to word-final position; fn.7: 'Secondary stress has never been reported for Kaqchikel.. it seems safest to assume that there is no word-level secondary stress at all in Kaqchikel' (lax vowels and [ʔC] clusters limited to stressed final syllables). Language-level.

sources.citation: García Matzar, Pedro (Lolmay) & José Obispo Rodríguez Guaján (Pakal B'alam). 1997 [reimpr. 2001]. Rukemik ri Kaqchikel chi': Gramática kaqchikel. Guatemala: Cholsamaj / OKMA. pp. 20-21.
sources.note: p.20: Kaqchikel has fixed stress, 'agudo', always on the final syllable of the word (root, derived or compound); enclitics attract stress; p.21: Spanish loans keep grave/esdrújula stress (kaxa, xara, anma), native exceptions nana, tata, Comalapa janila. Santa María de Jesús mentioned only for diphthongs ie/uo (scanned l.957, 2436) and retained final -j (l.2312), not for stress. Language-level (authors' dialects Tecpán, San Andrés Semetabaj).

sources.note: 'Both K'ekchi and Cakchiquel have fixed final stress'; Cakchiquel speakers from Patzicía. Language-level (basis of the existing kaqc1270 catalog entry).

sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2016. Mayan phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10(10): 469-514. doi:10.1111/lnc3.12148, sec. 6.1 p.495.
sources.note: 'Final stress (36a) is the norm in K'ichean languages'; 'Kaqchikel, for instance, follows the typical K'ichean pattern of final stress, but non-final stress occurs in both loanwords (anima) and in some native words (janila)'. Language-level; Santa María de Jesús not mentioned (only Santa María Cauqué vowels).

sources.note: Orthographic norm; 'acento' appears only in the loanword section (~p.298: some loans are 'graves' with penultimate stress: anx, anm, xalma, nan, tata, xara, paxa; others 'agudas' with final stress: patix, kape', karne'l, turas). Santa María de Jesús mentioned for diphthongs (p.38: 'Aunque en Santa María de Jesús, Sacatepéquez se utilicen todas las palabras anteriores con diptongo, para la escritura práctica no se sugiere escribirlo'); no SMJ stress statement.
